title: Addressing Modes
body:
### Register Direct
* Specify an operation directly on a register
* source and destination are both registers (dN or aN)
ex: ```
```
move.l     d0,d1 
;src  -> register direct
;dest -> register direct
```

dest=reg direct`

### Immediate
* The operand is a specific data value 
* data value is indicated by #
* Destination is never immediate
ex: ``
```
move.l    #5,d1
;src  -> immediate
;dest -> register direct

movea.l   #var,a1
;src  -> immediate (data value IS the address of var)
;dest -> register direct
```

### Absolute
* data value is found at directly specified address
* Identified by numeric value or label
ex: 
```
move.l    5,d1 
;src  -> absolute (data value CONTAINED in adress 5)
;dest -> register direct

movea.l   var,a1  
;src  -> absolute
;dest -> register direct
```

### Register Indirect
* Sort of like dereferencing pointers
* identified by parenthesis 
ex:
``` 
		move.l   #var,a0
		move.b   (a0),d2    ;copies 99 into d2
		;src  -> register indirect ()
		;dest -> register direct

var:    dc.b     99         ;this is a pointer!
```
`-(sp)` and `(sp)+` are two more, pre-decrement and post-increment register indirect; they
are how you push and pop, see [[Subroutines]].
